shared_elements: rounded knob/boss form (A's head knob; B's disc-like shapes in upper band)
wing rendered with repeated parallel ridges/lines
justification: Both objects are pale stone carvings whose most legible motif is a bird in profile with a heavy hooked beak and a wing built from repeated parallel ridges, and both include rounded boss-like elements. But A is a single free-standing figure carved fully in the round with no surrounding imagery, while B is a flat slab covered with a multi-register low-relief composition of bands, quadrupeds and stacked creatures, so the arrangement and carving technique differ fundamentally.
